records.name: Millsburg Liberia Development Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that gives computers to children from low-income families so they can do schoolwork and learn about technology. It also promotes education and training in struggling communities.
records.what_you_do: Donate a computer that needs repair (the group fixes them for children), give money through the donate page, or call the office to ask about getting a computer for a child. You can also subscribe to updates on the website.

cost.text: No cost is listed on the site for receiving or donating a computer.

first_step.how: Call 267-888-0230 to ask about getting or donating a computer. The site also has a subscribe form for updates.
first_step.basis: The site has a phone line, a subscribe form and a donate page, but it does not say how families are chosen or what the steps are to get a computer.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit, office hours, or a meeting. The only listed ways to start are a phone call or the contact page, and the site lists no fee for receiving or donating a computer.
first_visit_tips: Call before you go, since the site lists no office hours.
The office is in the rear building at 6724 Elmwood Ave.

records.notes: The get-involved page covers donations only. No volunteer roles, office hours, or computer request steps are published. The footer copyright is the only year on the site, and the about page says the group began in 2010, so there is no dated news to set a status. The contact page lists a second phone line (267-884-8130) without saying what it is for, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Mishkan Shalom
records.summary: A Reconstructionist congregation in Roxborough with Shabbat services, a Hebrew school, a choir, a men's group, spiritual direction, and a Rosh Chodesh gathering.
records.what_you_do: Come to Saturday Shabbat services, in person or streamed on YouTube. Ask the office or the rabbi about membership, which Hebrew school requires. Choir, adult education, and the men's group are also listed on the site.

schedule.text: Shabbat services are held on Saturday mornings, about 10 am to noon, in person and streamed on YouTube. Hebrew school, adult education, and choir sessions are on the congregation's calendar.

cost.text: Dues are set by a self-assessed annual commitment level. The site prints no dollar amounts.

first_step.how: Email Rabbi Shawn Zevit at rabbishawn@mishkan.org or call the office at 215-508-0226 before a Saturday service to ask about visiting.
first_step.basis: Services and public events are listed with times and a clear contact route, and the page says prospective members meet the membership team first. The site does not say whether guests may attend Shabbat.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. Saturday Shabbat runs about 10 am to noon and is led by the rabbi and a student rabbi, in the building and on YouTube. The membership steps are spelled out, but the site does not say what a guest can do or whether a guest pays anything.
first_visit_tips: Email or call ahead to ask whether guests may come to services.
The office is at 4101 Freeland Ave. in Roxborough, open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm, and Friday by appointment.
Watch a Shabbat service on the congregation's YouTube channel first if you want a preview.

records.notes: Hebrew school enrollment is for members only, according to the school page. The site does not say whether guests may attend Shabbat, and it prints no dues amounts. Office hours are Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 4 pm, with Friday by appointment. The Acts of Caring page is for members' life events and asks people to email news; it does not describe open visitor participation, so it is not recorded as a first step.

records.name: Modero & Co.
records.summary: A community dance group founded in 2011 that shares Indonesian culture through dance and immersive public events. Its dancers perform at public festivals and community events, sometimes alongside gamelan music.
records.what_you_do: Watch the group's dance performances at festivals and community events, or use the subscribe box on the home page to hear about the next one.

schedule.text: Performances happen at public festivals and community events, and the home page lists upcoming ones. The site lists no weekly classes or regular meetings.

locations.label: Chestnut Hill venue (one listed event venue)

cost.text: The site does not state ticket prices or admission costs.

first_step.how: Use the subscribe box on modero.co to get on the list, then attend one of the public performances listed on the home page.
first_step.basis: Performances are public and listed, but the site has no classes, volunteer roles, or join route, only a subscribe box and a contact form, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit. Most listed events are performances you watch at festivals or community venues, usually in the afternoon or evening. Check the event details for cost and location before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the home page for the date, time, and address of the performance you plan to see.
Follow the group on Instagram or YouTube to see photos and clips from past performances.

records.notes: The site has no classes, volunteer, or join pages. Event dates on the home page print no year, so none is recorded. A web search found no 2026 listing for the group; the newest items it found are from 2024. The contact page lists a phone number and an email without saying what they are for, so they are not recorded. The listed Chestnut Hill venue is for one event, not a fixed meeting place.

records.name: Moishe House Philadelphia
records.summary: A Jewish young adult house in Philadelphia for people in their 20s and their friends. It hosts about seven events a month, such as talks, learning sessions, a Moishe Eats series, and holiday parties.
records.what_you_do: Email the house or use the contact form to ask about an event, then come to a gathering such as a talk, a nigun circle, or a tasting.

schedule.text: The house hosts about seven events a month, at the house and around the city. Most gatherings run in the evening, about 6 to 9 pm.

cost.text: The national FAQ says programs are free, though a local event may need a ticket.

first_step.how: Email moishehousephilly@gmail.com or use the contact form on the house's Find a House page to ask about the next event.
first_step.basis: The house page says to contact the house to attend, and the national FAQ says you can come even if you know no one and that residents will welcome you. No formal newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: The house does not describe a first event. Gatherings usually run in the evening, from about 6 to 9 pm, and are hosted by the residents, who are young adults. The house does not publish its address, so you need to contact it to learn where an event meets.
first_visit_tips: Email the house before you go so you get the address and event details.
The national FAQ says you do not need to be Jewish to attend.

records.notes: Event listings on the house page show a day and time but no year, so no year is recorded and status stays probably_active. The national FAQ describes Moishe Houses in general, not this house alone. The national contact page lists no Philadelphia house contact, so it is not used as a source. The house page calls its audience Jewish 20-somethings, while the FAQ says non-Jews may attend.

records.name: Mom Your Business
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps Black and Brown women start and grow businesses in the Philadelphia region, with office hours, skill-building, and help getting funding.
records.what_you_do: Book an office hour for one-on-one business help, take part in networking and skill-building events, or use FounderyPHL, the group's interactive map of local business resources.

schedule.text: Office hours run every Tuesday and Thursday, 1 to 5 pm. Sessions are booked through the website's contact page.

first_step.how: Request an office hour through the contact page on momyourbusiness.com, which lists Tuesday and Thursday sessions from 1 to 5 pm.
first_step.basis: The way to book is clear and public, but the mission centers on Black and Brown women founders, and the site does not say who may book office hours or what a session costs.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a session. It says office hours are on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons and that you book through the website. It does not say how long a session lasts, whether it costs money, or whether the office is open to walk-ins.
first_visit_tips: Ask in your request whether office hours are open to you and what a session costs.
The office is at 348 E Walnut Lane, #4, in the 19144 zip code.
Call 800-524-4934 if you need help booking.

records.notes: Office hours were not in the tier 1 data and are now published on the contact page (Tuesday and Thursday, 1 to 5 pm). The events page lists no upcoming events and no event dates. The mission text says the group serves Black and Brown women founders; the only community tag used is women, since the cheat sheet has no single tag for that group. The site does not say whether the FounderyPHL map is open to everyone, so that wording is not repeated. Partners named on the site, such as 1 Million Cups and Phirst Market Ventures, have no URL on the site, so they are not added as leads.

records.name: Moonstone Arts Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts nonprofit founded in 1981 that focuses on literature. It runs about 100 programs a year, mostly poetry readings, and publishes books through Moonstone Press. Some events are free.
records.what_you_do: Attend a public reading, or read your own poem at an open reading when the event offers one. The center also lists intern and volunteer roles in publishing, design, film, and grant research.

schedule.text: The center holds about 100 reading events a year and lists them by date on its events page. Readings are held at the center and at other venues, such as Fergie's Pub.

cost.text: Some events are free. The site does not show prices for other events.

first_step.how: Pick a public reading from the events page and come along. To read at an open reading, call the center at 215-735-9600 and ask how to sign up.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly with dates and venues, so anyone can come. The site does not explain how to sign up for an open reading.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most events are poetry readings by featured poets, and some include an open reading or open mic. The site does not say how to sign up to read, so ask first if you want a turn. Check the event page for the venue and whether it is free.
first_visit_tips: Check the event page for the venue, since events are held at the center, at Fergie's Pub, and at other spots.
Ask the center by phone how to sign up before you plan to read.
The center posts recent readings on its YouTube channel if you want a preview.

records.notes: Open reading sign-up and time limits are not published anywhere on the site. The events page shows 2026 next to its listings: Oct 13 is a broadcast, Oct 14 and Oct 21 are at Fergie's Pub (Oct 21 is free), and Oct 17 is at Perch Music and Arts Workshop. These dates are not written into schedule text. The intern and volunteer page mentions the pandemic and gives no date, so its details may be out of date. The page's contact email for intern applications is not recorded.

records.name: Morris Animal Refuge
records.summary: A Philadelphia animal welfare group, founded in 1874, that runs adoptions, a community cat program, and a Philly Pets program. It also places animals in foster homes and uses shelter volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at the shelter (age 14 and up) or in the PetSmart cat role (age 18 and up), or foster an animal in your home until it is ready for a new family. Start with the interest form for the role you want.

schedule.text: Adoption hours are Tuesday and Saturday noon to 5 pm, and Wednesday and Friday noon to 7 pm. Shelter volunteer shifts depend on the role, and PetSmart shifts run about three hours.

first_step.how: Fill out the shelter interest form on the volunteer page, or the Under 18 form if you are 14 to 17. To foster, complete the foster questionnaire or application on the foster page. Volunteer questions go to volunteer@morrisanimalrefuge.org.
first_step.basis: The way in is clear (an interest form and then a volunteer waiver), but the volunteer page notes a waitlist dated January 2025, and foster applicants complete counseling before a first pet. An application step comes before you see what it is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical shift. Shelter volunteers may help with animal care, dog walks, cat socialization, photos and animal bios, transport, or fundraising events, depending on the role. Because the volunteer page noted a waitlist dated January 2025, ask about the current wait before you plan to start.
first_visit_tips: Read the volunteer waiver linked on the volunteer page before your first shift.
Adoption hours are listed on the site, so you can plan a visit to see the animals at 1242 Lombard Street.
If you are under 18, plan for an adult to supervise, since the page says minors may need it.

records.notes: The foster page does not state a minimum age, home rules, training, time commitment, or cost. The volunteer page says there is a waitlist for the main shelter program, dated January 2025. The home page prints full 2026 dates on its news posts (the newest is September 28, 2026), and the events page prints no years. Ages 14 to 17 volunteer through a separate Under 18 form, and minors may need an adult present. Questions about fostering a specific animal go to a foster address on the foster page, not recorded here. The PetSmart cat role is in South Philadelphia and its address is not published.
